comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the watchdog poll timer busy-spins ~1 core for the entire lifetime of every attempt**

The new watchdog uses `read -t 1 -u 3` with fd 3 opened from `/dev/zero` as its 1-second poll timer (`scripts/load_drop_retry.sh:170` + `:181`, reused at `:195`/`:199` for the drain loop). `read` on `/dev/zero` never blocks and never yields a newline, so the builtin loops on instant `read()` syscalls for the full second — this is a hot poll loop, not a timer.

Measured on this checkout (the real script, stubbed runner):

- 30 s wall run with a sleeping stub: **30.25 CPU-seconds consumed** (8.20 user + 22.05 sys) ≈ one full core pinned for the whole run.
- Sampled at 3 s elapsed: the wrapper bash at **99.3% CPU** (`ps -o pcpu`), while the stub itself slept at ~0%.

Why it matters: this watchdog now runs on every attempt of every wrapped leg — the PTY integration shards (ci.yml:1470), the core unit shards (ci.yml:1011), the jsr trio (ci.yml:1047), and the local fast gate (ci_fast_gate.sh:252). A healthy shard run pays one pinned core for its full duration (a 5-min shard ≈ 5 core-minutes stolen), and the PTY legs are precisely the load-sensitive class (FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE, "SM dispatch waves pack the hosted pool") whose flakes this PR heals — the fix adds sustained CPU contention to the conditions that induce the failure.

The intent behind `/dev/zero` ("killing this subshell mid-wait forks no `sleep` child for the job harness to report") can be kept with a true zero-CPU, zero-child timer: open a watchdog-private FIFO `O_RDWR` — `exec 3<>"${CONSOLE}.wdg.fifo"` — an O_RDWR fifo never EOFs (the process's own write end holds it), so `read -t 1 -u 3` blocks silently until the timeout. Verified in this sandbox: 3 × `read -t 1` polls = 3009 ms elapsed, **0.00 CPU** (`/usr/bin/time`: 0% of wall). Add the fifo to the existing `cleanup` trap. (Do NOT point fd 3 at the console fifo itself — reading it would steal the runner's output from `tee`.)

Alternatively `sleep 1` would also work but forks the child you deliberately avoided, so the fifo timer is the closer match to the stated constraint. The ≤1 s drain loop at `:195` is bounded and can keep the `/dev/zero` form or take the same fix.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
# Re: ⚠️ IMPORTANT — the watchdog poll timer busy-spins ~1 core for the entire lifetime of every attempt

Fixed on this head. The `/dev/zero` fd-3 timer is gone; the watchdog now blocks on your
zero-CPU, zero-child sketch exactly as verified in the thread.

## What changed (`scripts/load_drop_retry.sh`)

- **Timer fifo** (`scripts/load_drop_retry.sh:168-169` + `:201`): `run_streamed` creates a
  watchdog-private fifo `mkfifo "${CONSOLE}.wdg.fifo"` and the watchdog subshell opens it
  `exec 3<>"$WDOG_FIFO"` (O_RDWR — the process's own write end holds it, so it never EOFs).
  `read -t 1 -u 3` now **blocks silently for the whole second at zero CPU** instead of spinning
  on instant `read()` syscalls. Your "do NOT point fd 3 at the console fifo" constraint is
  respected — the timer fifo is a separate file, and the console fifo keeps its single reader
  (`tee`).
- **Cleanup** (`scripts/load_drop_retry.sh:120-122` + `:236-238`): the fifo is removed by the
  existing `cleanup` trap AND at the end of every `run_streamed` call, so no fifo node is ever
  left behind on any path (normal, wedge-kill, or trap exit).
- **Drain loop** (`scripts/load_drop_retry.sh:227-233`): the ≤1 s drain window takes the same
  fifo fix (fd 3 opened on the same timer fifo, closed after the loop), so no `/dev/zero`
  `read -t` form remains in the script.
- The `read -t`-as-builtin rationale is preserved: killing the watchdog subshell mid-wait still
  forks no `sleep` child for the job harness to report — the fifo replaces only the timer's
  data source.

## Measured on this fix (real script, sleeping stub, `/usr/bin/time` over the wrapper tree)

- Before (round-2 head): 3 s wall → **3.21 CPU-s** (1.36 user + 1.85 sys) ≈ 107% of one core.
- After: 3 s wall → **0.02 CPU-s** (0.01 + 0.01). No `sleep` child forked, no stray children.

## Regression test (TDD)

`test/scripts/load_drop_retry_test.dart` **AC25** runs the real wrapper under
`/usr/bin/time` with a 3-s sleeping stub and asserts (a) wrapper-tree CPU < 50% of wall
(the busy-spin fails it at ~100%, the fix passes at ~0.6%), and (b) the run exits green with a
single invocation. It failed on the pre-fix head (3.22 CPU-s / 3.23 s wall) and passes now.

Also healed the two digest items from your ranked list while in the file:

- **`load_drop_retry.sh:171` stderr leak** — the spam baseline is now computed in
  `run_streamed`'s parent scope *before* `tee` starts (`:149-161`): a fresh first invocation has
  no `wc -c <` redirect to fail (AC25 asserts no `No such file or directory` on stderr), and the
  baseline-after-start undercount window is closed. Note the fresh (non-append) run truncates the
  console, so its baseline is 0; the `--append` rerun baseline is the pre-append size — the AC24
  no-insta-kill contract is unchanged and still green.
- **`grep: write error: Broken pipe`** noise when the watchdog subshell is killed mid-pipeline —
  the spam-count `grep` in the watchdog now silences its own stderr (`:204`); reproduced the
  noise on the old head, gone on this one.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The gh-2381 healing design is sound and evidence-driven — I verified against the real test-core reporter that compile errors and nonexistent targets always emit `suite` events (so `NEVER_LOADED` only arms on genuine engine abandonment), and all 33 changed-file tests pass locally. One important issue gates: the new watchdog's `/dev/zero` `read -t` poll timer is a busy-loop that pins ~1 core for the entire lifetime of every attempt (measured 99.3% CPU), adding sustained contention to the exact load-sensitive PTY legs this PR heals.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ `scripts/load_drop_retry.sh:170` — watchdog timer busy-spins ~1 core per attempt (thread with measurements + verified zero-CPU fix sketch)

Ranked digest (below thread threshold):
- `scripts/load_drop_retry.sh:171` — stderr noise on every fresh first invocation: `wc -c < "$CONSOLE"` redirect error leaks (`2>/dev/null` cannot apply to the failing redirect; reproduced twice in sandbox smoke runs) — compute the baseline in `run_streamed`'s parent scope before starting `tee` (also removes the small baseline-after-start undercount window)
- `scripts/load_drop_retry.sh` — occasional `grep: write error: Broken pipe` stderr noise when the watchdog subshell is killed mid-pipeline (observed once); cosmetic
- `test/scripts/load_drop_retry_test.dart` AC22 — the in-flight suite `test/inflight_test.dart` is not among the invocation targets; real in-flight suites always are, so a targets-consistent fixture would pin the tighter contract (wrapper tolerates it fine)

**Next Steps**:
1. Replace the watchdog's `/dev/zero` fd-3 timer with a private O_RDWR fifo (`exec 3<>"${CONSOLE}.wdg.fifo"` + cleanup) — zero CPU, still no child processes (verified in sandbox); add the fifo to the cleanup trap
2. Move the watchdog baseline computation ahead of the `tee` start to silence the line-171 stderr leak
